# Turn 1: Empty frame rule amendment batch

**Decoding the grant.** The header has exactly one `**Amend-grant:**` line. Its value `2 more fix rounds` matches the budget token once, with N=2. Removing the token leaves nothing, so this grant funds rounds only. It gives no amend permission.

So I take the ordinary path through steps 2-4:

- **Prefilter.** The item edits `## Acceptance criteria`, which is a human-owned section. It goes straight to the human batch.
- **No reviewer dispatch.** There is no `documentation-impact.md` resolution and no `spec-council-member` call.
- **No edits yet.** Nothing is edited and nothing is committed. The working tree stays as it is until the human replies.
- **No tracker calls.** I make no `plan_tracker` or `phase_tracker` call before the reply.

The plan clause comes from the plan file and tracker state. Task 3 is `in_progress`, not complete, so applying the recommendation reopens no completed tasks.

```
Spec amendments: 1 need your call - from the implement phase; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Empty frame rule - the acceptance criteria state how empty frames are handled: empty payloads are rejected, heartbeat markers are still permitted. Task 3 cannot validate frames against an acceptance criterion that leaves empty frames undefined.
   Only you can change the acceptance criteria.
   Example: empty frame -> rejected unless it is a heartbeat marker
   Reviewer: not reviewed - acceptance-criteria location
   Impact: Acceptance criteria: empty-frame handling unspecified -> empty payloads rejected, heartbeat markers accepted
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text: zero-length frames are permitted
   B) alt-1 - every empty frame is rejected, heartbeat markers included
   C) alt-2 - empty payloads are rejected, heartbeat markers are permitted
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: C - closes the empty-frame gap without breaking heartbeat keepalives

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
empty: Acceptance criteria - old: <current approved empty-frame criterion text, verbatim> -> new: <alt-2 criterion text, verbatim>
```

The turn ends here.

---

# Independent continuation: human chose alt-2, aftermath done, header still `2 more fix rounds`

The recorded line was already printed as part of the completed batch: `Recorded: empty=alt-2`.

## Where the CR loop stands

- Review 3 was `FIX_FIRST` with `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING`. That called for escalation.
- The single escalated round has run. Its CR re-review is still `FIX_FIRST`, with `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)`, so it is not `STAGNANT`.
- Per `fix-loop.md`, a re-review with issues after the escalated round gets a funded round while one remains for the task.
- The convergence exception is not re-armed by funding.

## Before dispatch

1. Re-read and re-decode the header `**Amend-grant:** 2 more fix rounds`. It still funds N=2 with no amend permission.
2. Task 3's ledger shows 0 spent, since no funded round has run.
3. Touched owners: the fix targets `src/frame.ts`, which task 3 owns, and task 3 is the only task in the wave. Task 3 is not exhausted.
4. Print:

```
funded round 1 of 2 for task 3
```

## Funded round 1: in-place repair, no fan-out, no worktree flag

This is the integrated wave before its commit, so the repair runs in place in the branch checkout. The payload repeats the escalated round's payload and isolation exactly.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<Task 3 "Validate frame" full text, verbatim>
<task Spec: anchors - read from the amended spec at its absolute path; acceptance criteria now carry alt-2: empty payloads rejected, heartbeat markers permitted>
<Leg: / Rules: context, if any>
<prior escalated patch>
Work from: /workspace/project

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <task 3's Tests: block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<the escalated round's CR re-review report, complete and verbatim, ending
 Behaviour-change: no
 TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)
 including: src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard>

<status protocol verbatim: **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT ...>`
})
```

The payload contains no commit or staging instruction. The observed result is `DONE`.

## Scoped test gate on the integrated tree

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test frame.test.mjs)
```

This is observed to pass.

## Stage the repair and record tree-after for the Fix delta

Run in the branch checkout, because this is an integrated review:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

```bash
FD_ROOT=/workspace/project
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

The printed SHA becomes `<tree-after>`, keyed to this wave. `<tree-before>` is the wave tree recorded when the escalated round's CR re-review was dispatched.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>
```

The delta is nonempty per the observation, so the re-review goes ahead.

## CR re-review

`Behaviour-change: no`, so this is a CR re-review only, with the same `WAVE_BASE_SHA` and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` as before.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: Task 3 "Validate frame" - funded repair of the missing length guard (src/frame.ts:21)
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <wave task 3 from the plan, with the amended acceptance criteria>
BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs
<Leg: / Rules: context, if any>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<escalated round's CR re-review report, complete and verbatim>

<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md "Re-review: trajectory verdict", verbatim>

## Fix delta
<output of git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>>`
})
```

The observed verdict is **`SHIP`**. That is a clean review, so the loop ends. I dispatch no funded round 2, and I do not carry this report's Minors.

## Step 7: wave commit, then complete

1. Fold the worker commits and all remaining changes into one wave commit:

   ```bash
   git -C /workspace/project reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" && git -C /workspace/project add -A && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 3: validate frame"
   ```

2. If that commit turns out empty, stop instead of completing the task.

3. After a non-empty commit, mark task 3 complete:

   ```ts
   plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <task 3's tracker index>, status: "complete" })
   ```

4. The tree is now clean for the next wave. Task 3 was never complete before this commit.

**Caution to surface, not resolve:** if the amendment aftermath's `amend:` commit landed on top of `WAVE_BASE_SHA` during this wave, `reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA"` would fold that commit into the wave commit. Its `amend:` subject, which `finishing-a-development-branch` Step 4 greps for, would be lost. Check `git -C /workspace/project log --oneline "$WAVE_BASE_SHA"..HEAD` before committing, and raise it with the user if an `amend:` commit appears.

The wave boundary has been reached; I stop here.

## Turn 1 — amendment gate; stop for the human

`2 more fix rounds` grants **two funded fixes, not permission to amend the spec**. This changes a human-owned acceptance contract, so it goes directly to the human menu. No amendment, fix, or review is dispatched yet.

The exact existing acceptance-criterion text was not included in this replay. Below, `<existing AC text verbatim>` denotes that available text, not a reconstructed criterion.

Spec amendments: 1 need your call - from the implement phase; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Empty frame rule - distinguish empty payloads from heartbeat markers. This makes the empty-frame validation contract explicit.
   Only you can change the acceptance criterion.
   Example: empty payload and heartbeat marker both accepted -> empty payload rejected; heartbeat marker permitted
   Reviewer: not reviewed - acceptance-criteria location
   Impact: Acceptance criteria: existing empty-frame rule -> reject empty payloads but permit heartbeat markers
   A) accept - permit zero-length frames
   B) alt-1 - reject all empty frames
   C) alt-2 - reject empty payloads but permit heartbeat markers
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: C - preserves heartbeat markers while rejecting empty payloads

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details  
empty: ## Acceptance criteria - old: `<existing AC text verbatim>` -> new: reject empty payloads but permit heartbeat markers

**This turn ends here, awaiting the human response.**

---

## Independent continuation — fixed human choice and completed aftermath

For this continuation only, take the supplied observations as given: the human chose `alt-2`, amendment aftermath is complete, and the header remains:

```text
**Amend-grant:** 2 more fix rounds
```

The ordinary loop and its single escalation have already run. The latest escalated CR remains `FIX_FIRST`; its divergence does not grant another ordinary fix or escalation. Funding is available independently: task 3 has spent **0 of 2**.

All commands and dispatches below are proposed next actions, not execution claims. Angle-bracket insertions refer to the available verbatim artifacts or recorded values.

### 1. Dispatch funded fix 1, in place

Print before dispatch:

```text
funded round 1 of 2 for task 3
```

Dispatch one worker—no fan-out and no nested worktree. Preserve the recorded `WAVE_BASE_SHA`, even if the amendment aftermath added a commit.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
You are implementing a funded repair for Task 3: Validate frame.

## Task Description
<full current task 3 text verbatim>

## Context
<existing task context, applicable Leg and Rules, and spec anchors verbatim>
Read the applicable Rules files before acting.
The approved empty-frame contract is now: reject empty payloads but permit heartbeat markers.
Repair the current integrated implementation in /workspace/project.
This is funded round 1 of 2 for task 3.
Do not commit; the orchestrator commits the wave only after acceptance.

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test frame.test.mjs

TEST_CONTRACT:
<task 3 Tests block and Create/Test paths verbatim>

## Prior patch
<existing repair payload's prior patch verbatim>

## Previous review report
<complete escalated CR re-review report verbatim, including:
FIX_FIRST, its finding at src/frame.ts:21, Behaviour-change: no,
and its TRAJECTORY line>

<status protocol verbatim: explicitly return DONE,
DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED>
`
})
```

This dispatch spends one funded round. Under the fixed observation, it returns `DONE` with a nonempty tracked delta.

### 2. Run the parent scoped gate

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test frame.test.mjs)
```

Proceed only on success. The scenario fixes that result as passing.

### 3. Stage and record the re-review tree

The delta’s **before** tree is the recorded tree from the escalated CR re-review’s dispatch—not `WAVE_BASE_SHA` and not a newly substituted working-tree diff.

Run this entire block in one shell invocation:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" add -A || exit 1

FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Record the printed SHA as this wave’s current CR review tree. Generate the payload’s delta using the two recorded tree SHAs:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary \
  '<tree recorded at escalated CR re-review dispatch>' \
  '<tree printed by the block above>'
```

A shell failure stops dispatch. The supplied nonempty-delta observation avoids the empty-delta failure route.

### 4. Dispatch the funded CR re-review

`Behaviour-change: no` means **CR only**, with no SR-first reroute. Review the integrated wave against its original base, including staged and unstaged changes.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review production readiness using the supplied code-reviewer template.
Read applicable Rules files before acting.

DESCRIPTION:
<integrated wave implementation summary and funded repair summary>

PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
<full current task 3 text, applicable Leg and Rules, and requirements verbatim>

BASE_SHA: <recorded WAVE_BASE_SHA>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test frame.test.mjs

The parent scoped gate passed after the repair.
Review the current integrated checkout against BASE_SHA, including staged
and unstaged changes. Do not review only the fix delta.

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<complete escalated CR re-review report verbatim>

If your task contains a "Previous review report (re-review trigger)" section
and you found issues, append exactly one more line after Behaviour-change: —
this line, not Behaviour-change:, is the true final line of the report:

TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (<n_prev> -> <n_now>, max severity <X>)
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING
TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT (repeat of: <finding>)

Pick the first label that applies, in this order:

1. STAGNANT: a previous Critical or Moderate finding survives materially unchanged — name it.
2. DIVERGING: <n_now> >= <n_prev>, or the fix introduced a new Critical or Moderate finding.
3. CONVERGING: otherwise — the Critical/Moderate count fell, no new Critical or
   Moderate appeared, and every surviving Critical or Moderate was materially improved.

<n_prev>/<n_now> count Critical and Moderate findings only; Minors — ride-along
Minors declined or unchanged, and (outside fix delta) downgrades alike — never
move the TRAJECTORY: line. <X> is the highest remaining severity. For this line
the severity set is exactly Critical/Moderate/Minor, regardless of the vocabulary
used elsewhere in your report.

The orchestrator dispatches one extra fix only when this line says CONVERGING
without "max severity Critical" — be accurate, not generous.

If you found no issues, report success as usual and omit this line.
First reviews (no previous-report section) omit this line.

## Fix delta
<verbatim binary diff between the recorded prior and current review trees>
`
})
```

### 5. Consume the supplied `SHIP`; commit the wave

The scenario supplies `SHIP` for this re-review. That ends the loop, regardless of any Minors. **Do not dispatch funded round 2.** Task 3 remains `in_progress` until the durable wave commit succeeds.

Run with the original recorded base substituted:

```bash
WAVE_BASE_SHA='<recorded WAVE_BASE_SHA>'
git -C "/workspace/project" reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" &&
git -C "/workspace/project" add -A &&
git -C "/workspace/project" commit -m "Validate frame lengths and heartbeat markers"
```

Stop on failure or an empty commit; do not complete the task in either case. After a successful commit, confirm the checkout is clean:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" status --porcelain
```

Then mark the existing task index complete:

```ts
plan_tracker({
  action: "update",
  index: 3,
  status: "complete"
})
```

**Boundary: wave committed and task 3 completed. No further funding, verification-phase actions, or finishing dispatches are proposed.**
